subject: Crescent Analytics — proof-of-host ledger and certificate escrow request
messages:
From: Samir Patel <security@crescentanalytics.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@crescentanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Crescent Analytics — on-prem hostname proof and certificate escrow

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re moving toward a pilot of Redwood Private in our on-prem environment and security needs some concrete artifacts before we can green-light deployment. Two asks from compliance:

1) A ledger or documented proof-of-hostname workflow showing how hostname ownership is asserted for private FQDNs (we need to show auditors the chain of custody for FQDN claims).
2) Options and controls for "certificate escrow" or otherwise ensuring that Crescent can recover TLS material and audit issuance for long-lived private endpoints (we’re a regulated vertical and need key-recovery / escrow options documented).

Specifically, can you provide:
- A short runbook or diagram of the hostname attestation flow for on-prem hosts (CSR -> signing -> distribution) that we can include in our inventory.
- A template for a cert inventory we can fill out.
- A description of Redwood's supported escrow modes (Redwood-managed escrow, customer-managed HSM/KMS, hybrid) plus the audit evidence generated.
- Any constraints for on-prem (air-gapped) installs.

If you can share an example CSR/attestation header and a timeline for a short workshop to walk our security/procurement teams through options, that would be ideal.

We’re aiming to present to auditors the week of Jan 26 — is that feasible?

Thanks,
Samir Patel
InfoSec Manager, Crescent Analytics
[Attachment: example-csr.pem (text)]
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <security@crescentanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Crescent Analytics — on-prem hostname proof and certificate escrow

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can provide all three items and run a focused workshop. Below is a concise plan and attachments to get started.

What I’m attaching now:
- cert-inventory-template.csv — blank inventory we ask customers to fill (FQDN, intended runtime, TTL, private/public, issuing CA, expiry, intended rotation cadence).
- tls-escrow-options.pdf — a short summary of supported escrow patterns and tradeoffs.
- mutual-tls-checklist.pdf — operational checklist for mutual-TLS endpoints and on-prem constraints.

High-level attestation patterns we support (short):
1) Customer-managed KMS/HSM + Redwood CA: Customer stores CA signing key material in their HSM and uses an enrollment flow; Redwood signs using an attestable signing operation (logs + audit). Good for regulated customers who require key custody.
2) Redwood-managed escrow (audited): Redwood holds encrypted private keys in a secure escrow vault (KMS-wrapped) with documented access procedures and two-person approval for recovery. We provide audit trail (who requested recovery, timestamps, exported cert PEMs, and justification).
3) Ephemeral CSR + ACME sidecar for short-lived certs: For many private endpoints we recommend ephemeral certificates (short TTL) and automated renewal; proof-of-hostness is done via a signed enrollment token tied to a host identity provider (e.g., SAML/OIDC or a verified CSR signer).

We’ll prepare:
- A diagram of CSR lifecycle for on-prem hosts (CSR generation, nonce attestation, CA signing, distribution, and revocation).
- A sample attestation header (human- and machine-readable) you can store in your ledger.
- A mapping of evidence artifacts (audit logs, DocIDs, signed CSRs) to compliance questions.

Workshop proposal: 60 minutes (30m overview, 30m Q&A + procurement/compliance breakout). Dates I can offer: Jan 20 (AM PT), Jan 22 (PM PT), Jan 27 (AM PT). Please confirm stakeholders you want in the breakout (procurement / legal / infra ops).

Ben — can you pull the latest CA trust matrix and a short note on our typical rotation cadences for private certs?
Karthik — please sketch the enrollment options we support for air-gapped installs (offline CSR puller / USB seed / signed attestation token).

Samir — attaching the templates now. Once you populate the inventory with a few sample FQDNs we’ll prepare the diagram and sample headers.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Product Security Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: cert-inventory-template.csv]
[Attachment: tls-escrow-options.pdf]
From: Samir Patel <security@crescentanalytics.com>

Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@crescentanalytics.com>

Grace — this is helpful, thanks. We’ll fill the inventory (attaching a preliminary list) and get back with preferred workshop date.

A couple quick clarifications for the workshop:
- Please include someone who can speak to audit evidence exports (format, retention windows, and who in Redwood can request/export escrowed keys).
- On the customer-managed KMS option: we need a clear list of supported HSM/KMS vendors and any integration pre-reqs (networking, ports, credentials).

We have a compliance lockbox team and procurement lead who should be present in the breakout. I’ll propose Jan 27 AM PT if that works — gives us time to populate the inventory.

Thanks,
Samir
[Attachment: crescent-prelim-inventory.csv]
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Samir — Jan 27 AM PT works for us. We’ll run the 60-minute workshop and include:
- Ben: CA trust matrix, retention/audit export workflow, typical rotation windows.
- Karthik: air-gap enrollment patterns (offline CSR puller, signed token import) and network pre-reqs for customer-managed KMS.
- Me: attestation ledger format, sample CSR headers, and the escrow recovery process (who signs off, SLAs, and audit trail).

Pre-work: please upload the filled cert-inventory-template.csv to the Drive link I shared (I added write access for security@crescentanalytics.com). If you can also flag any FQDNs that will be on an air-gapped network we’ll tailor the flow.

Ben — assigned to you to attach the CA trust matrix + a 1-slide export spec for logs before the workshop. Karthik — can you prepare a short list of supported KMS/HSM vendors and the minimal network ports we’ll need to reach them from a Redwood Private node (or one-way export options for air-gapped setups)?

I’ve also created a compliance playbook draft in the Drive folder and a DocuSign envelope for an escrow agreement if you decide on Redwood-managed escrow — link in related_links.

See you on Jan 27.

Best,
Grace
[Attachment: mutual-tls-checklist.pdf]
